questions.prompt: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.hint: It lies in the country's south-central highlands.
questions.explanation: Nairobi is Kenya's capital.

questions.prompt: Mars was the Roman god of what?
questions.hint: His Greek counterpart was Ares.
questions.explanation: Mars was the Roman god of war.

questions.prompt: Carthage was founded by settlers from which people?
questions.hint: Its legendary founder was Dido of Tyre.
questions.explanation: Carthage began as a Phoenician colony.

questions.prompt: The Silk Road was best understood as what?
questions.hint: It linked many regions rather than following one road.
questions.explanation: The Silk Road was a changing network of overland and maritime routes.

questions.prompt: Tea cultivation originated in which country?
questions.hint: Early traditions connect it with Yunnan and Sichuan.
questions.explanation: Tea originated in China before spreading widely.

questions.prompt: Constantinople served as the Ottoman capital under what later common name?
questions.hint: The city straddles the Bosporus.
questions.explanation: Constantinople became widely known internationally as Istanbul.

questions.prompt: What is a lingua franca?

choices.text: A language spoken only in France
A common language used among people with different native languages

questions.hint: It facilitates trade and communication.
questions.explanation: A lingua franca is a bridge language between different speech communities.

questions.prompt: Arabic script is normally written in which direction?
questions.hint: Hebrew shares this orientation.
questions.explanation: Arabic is written from right to left.

questions.prompt: Which architectural feature is especially characteristic of Gothic churches?
questions.hint: Ribbed vaults and flying buttresses are also typical.
questions.explanation: Pointed arches are a hallmark of Gothic architecture.

questions.prompt: The 'Westphalian' model is commonly associated with what principle?
questions.hint: The concept is linked to the 1648 peace settlements.
questions.explanation: Westphalian sovereignty emphasizes states' authority within their territories.

questions.prompt: Mercantilism generally favored what?

choices.text: Accumulating national wealth through regulated trade and exports

questions.hint: Bullion and favorable trade balances were important.
questions.explanation: Mercantilist policies sought state power through controlled commerce and accumulated specie.

questions.prompt: Sikhism originated in which region?
questions.hint: Guru Nanak was born there.
questions.explanation: Sikhism arose in the Punjab region of South Asia.

questions.prompt: The Sahel lies immediately south of which desert?
questions.hint: It is a semi-arid transition zone.
questions.explanation: The Sahel stretches across Africa south of the Sahara.

questions.prompt: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in which city?
questions.hint: It took place in Yugoslavia in 1961.
questions.explanation: The first NAM summit met in Belgrade.

questions.prompt: The monumental stelae of Axum are found in which modern country?
questions.hint: Axum was a major ancient kingdom in the Horn of Africa.
questions.explanation: The famous Aksumite stelae stand in northern Ethiopia.

questions.prompt: What is 6 × 7?
questions.hint: Six groups of seven.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.hint: It is a one-letter symbol.
questions.explanation: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen.

questions.prompt: Earth is which planet from the Sun?
questions.hint: Venus is closer and Mars is farther.
questions.explanation: Earth is the third planet from the Sun.

questions.prompt: Why is ordinary RAM called volatile memory?

choices.text: It loses stored data when power is removed

questions.hint: Its contents require electrical power.
questions.explanation: Volatile memory does not retain data without power.

questions.prompt: What molecule stores most hereditary information in living organisms?
questions.hint: Its sequence encodes genes.
questions.explanation: DNA is the principal hereditary material in cellular life.

questions.prompt: What is 30% of 90?
questions.hint: Ten percent is 9.
questions.explanation: Three groups of 9 give 27.

questions.prompt: Ohm's law is commonly written as which equation?
questions.hint: Voltage equals current times resistance.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance as V = IR.

questions.prompt: What is the usual output of a cryptographic hash function?

choices.text: A reversible copy of the input

questions.hint: Inputs of many sizes map to outputs of one defined size.
questions.explanation: A hash function produces a fixed-length digest from arbitrary input.

questions.prompt: What is escape velocity?

choices.text: The minimum speed needed to escape a body's gravity without further propulsion
The speed of light in air
The rotation rate of a planet
The speed of a falling object at impact only

questions.hint: It depends on mass and distance from the body's center.
questions.explanation: Escape velocity is the threshold speed for an unpowered trajectory to reach infinity.

questions.prompt: Which fraction equals 0.125?
questions.hint: 125 thousandths simplifies.

questions.prompt: What is a photon?
questions.hint: Light can be described as packets of these.
questions.explanation: A photon is the quantum particle of the electromagnetic field.

questions.prompt: What is a mutex used for?

choices.text: Mutual exclusion around a shared resource

questions.hint: It prevents concurrent critical-section access.
questions.explanation: A mutex allows only one thread or process at a time to enter a protected section.

questions.prompt: What is a pulsar?

choices.text: A rotating neutron star observed through periodic beams

questions.hint: Its pulses can be extraordinarily regular.
questions.explanation: A pulsar is a magnetized rotating neutron star whose beams sweep past Earth.

questions.prompt: What is √2025?
questions.hint: 45 × 45 is just over 2000.

questions.prompt: Einstein's equivalence principle states that locally, uniform acceleration is indistinguishable from what?
questions.hint: An accelerating elevator provides the classic thought experiment.
questions.explanation: The equivalence principle links inertial acceleration and gravity locally.

sets.description: A mixed historical and cultural set connecting societies, languages, religions, trade routes, and political ideas.
